The cascade optimization strategy employs different optimization algorithms in a specified sequence.
The neural network and regression methods are used to approximate solutions obtained from the NASA Engine Performance Program (NEPP).
The new methodology is more robust and computationally efficient than the conventional optimization approach of using a single optimization algorithm with direct reanalysis.
The methodology is demonstrated on a preliminary design problem for a novel subsonic turbofan engine concept that incorporates a wave rotor as a cycle-topping device.
The computations of maximum thrust were obtained for a specific design point in the engine mission profile.
The results show a significant improvement in the maximum thrust obtained using the new cascade optimization methodology compared to benchmark solutions obtained using NEPP in a manual design mode.
The best performing optimization strategy is the Cascade 3 strategy, which uses an interspersed approach with NLPQ and neural network, FD and regression, and NLPQ with NEPP reanalysis.

The Cascade 1 strategy uses three algorithms: the Method of Feasible Directions (FD) followed by the Sequential Unconstrained Minimization Technique (SUMT) and the quadratic programming algorithm (NLPQ).
The authors are Dale A. Hopkins and Dr. Surya N. Patnaik from the NASA Glenn Research Center.
The research is part of the Propulsion System R&T program under the OAST Programs/Projects.
The novel subsonic turbofan engine concept incorporates a wave rotor as a cycle-topping device.
The benchmark solutions were obtained using NEPP in a manual design mode.
The cascade optimization strategies (Cascade 1, Cascade 2, and Cascade 3) are compared using both neural network and regression approximations.
The single optimization algorithm (NLPQ) is also compared using both neural network and regression approximations.
The results are depicted in a figure showing the optimum thrust for the subsonic wave-rotor-topped engine.
